 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER Case diary is available.

This is first application filed under Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant as he is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.575/2023 registered at Police Station Dabra Shahar, District Gwalior (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 376, 366, 323, 506 of IPC.
Prosecution case, in brief, is that the applicant and prosecutrix both are working in Gwalior Glory School, Shivpuri Link Road, Gwalior.
The applicant was Bus Driver, while the prosecutrix was working as a Helper.

On 01.06.2023 at about 07:00 hours, applicant on a false pretext of fill up a form, took her to Private Bus Stand, Gwalior and gave intoxicated tablet, due to which, she became unconscious, thereafter, the applicant committed sexual intercourse with her.

At about 12:00 hours,
when prosecutrix became conscious and started crying, then the applicant assaulted and threatened Deepak Joshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112603914/

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that admittedly, prosecutrix is a major lady.
Incident took place on 01.06.2023 while FIR has been lodged after about a month on 04.07.2023.
No plausible explanation was given in this regard.

It is further submitted that the applicant and prosecutrix were having relations with each other and when prosecutrix's husband came to know about their relations, she under the pressure of her husband lodged this false and fabricated FIR against the applicant.
He has submitted photographs of the applicant and prosecutrix in support of his submissions.
Under these circumstances, the applicant may be enlarged on anticipatory bail.
Learned counsel for the respondent/State has vehemently opposed the prayer and submits that due to the threats given by the applicant, prosecutrix could not lodge the FIR against him within time.
The prosecutrix in her statement specifically alleged about the acts of the applicant.
Offences alleged against the applicant are serious in nature, therefore, he is not entitled for bail.
Heard the learned counsel for both the parties.

Having considered the rival submissions, material pointed out by the learned counsel for the applicant, age of the prosecutrix, delayed FIR, so also other material produced on record, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that in the event of arrest of the applicant, he shall be released on bail upon furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Officer for his appearance before the Trial Court on all dates and for complying with the conditions enumerated in sub-section (2) of Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
Certified copy as per rules.

(SATYENDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE Abhi Deepak Joshi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/112603914/
